evidenceBoundaryZh: 该层补充候选级真实文献合成条件和 DOI，但文本挖掘字段仍需原文复核；数据集不提供统一产率、单位产品能耗、溶剂回收率或长期循环证据，因此这些字段继续作为比较性 LCA 的硬门控。
evidenceBoundaryEn: This layer adds candidate-level literature synthesis conditions and DOIs, but text-mined fields still require source-paper review. The dataset does not provide harmonized yield, energy per product, solvent recovery, or long-cycle evidence, so those remain hard gates for comparative LCA.

records.name: Cu(NO3)2·2.5H2O and NH4SCN
records.synthesisPrecaution: The preparation of this compound series afforded an opportunity to compare IR spectra . While it is generally recognized that νCN show lower frequency values and νSC exhibit higher values for N-bound thiocyanate complexes, these rules must be applied with caution because many other factors can exert influence on the positions of these bands [6] , [29] . All of the Cu(II) compounds prepared herein may be considered to bond to the metal through N, with additional weak S-bonding occurring in most cases (see below). IR spectra of complexes prepared herein and the free ligands are found in the Supporting Information . Notable IR bands are listed in Table 4 . Single νCN bands were observed in the range 2073–2097 cm−1 for all but five of the 21 complexes prepared. For the complexes of 3-MeOPy (10), 3-AcPy (12a), 4-NH2Py (17), Pdz (20), and Pyz (22) pairs of bands in the ranges of 2058–2073 cm−1 and 2104–2129 cm−1 were found. Thus, relatively high frequency CN bands were noted for all of the complexes studied. Such bands are more consistent with either S-bonding or N,S-bridging behavior (bands expected near 2100 cm−1) than with N-bound behavior (bands expected near 2050 cm−1) [6] , [29] . The νSC bands are challenging to identify because they are not particularly intense and tend to overlap with aromatic resonances. Comparison of complex and free XPy bands allowed for tentative identification of the νSC bands in the range 760–867 cm−1. This range is in good agreement with that recognized for N-bonded (760–860 cm−1) rather than S-bonded (690–720 cm−1) thiocyanate complexes.
records.conclusionBoundary: Real text-mined synthesis evidence; not a mass-balanced LCI and not a third-party-reviewed comparative LCA.

records.name: [Zn3(btc)2(H2O)8]·(H2O)4: C
records.synthesisPrecaution: Data were collected on a colourless rod (0.05 × 0.08 × 0.43 mm) at 123 K on a Nonius Kappa CCD diffractometer with graphite monochromated Mo-Kα radiation (λ = 0.71073 Å), using ϕ and ω rotations with 1° frames. The images were processed with the HKL suite of programs [18] . Solutions were obtained using shelxs -97 [19] followed by successive difference Fourier methods, and structures were refined against F2 using shelxl -97 [19] . Face-indexed absorption corrections were applied. The structure was refined in the non-centric space group Cc, but was refined as a racemic twin (twin ratio 0.7224:0.2776). No satisfactory solution could be found in the corresponding centrosymmetric space group C2/c. All non-hydrogen atoms were refined anisotropically. All aromatic hydrogen atoms were placed at geometric positions and not refined. The hydrogen atoms on the water ligands were found in the difference maps, and were refined freely apart from the constraint of not being closer than 0.84(1) Å to the oxygen atom. H11 refined to a position which was closer to a nearby hydrogen bound carboxylate oxygen (O333) of the uncoordinated H2btc− anion than to the water oxygen (O1). The hydrogen atoms on the carboxylate groups were not found, and consideration of the hydrogen bonding interactions and C–O bond distances could not distinguish between H2btc−/H2btc−, Hbtc2−/H3btc and H3btc/Hbtc2− alternatives, which will depend on the localised positions of the hydrogen atoms in the two hydrogen bonds between the coordinated and uncoordinated btc molecules. They have both nominally been assigned as H2btc−, however, this assignment should be treated with caution. The hydrogen atoms of the uncoordinated water molecules were also not found in the difference maps. Details of crystallographic data collection are listed in Table 1 .

records.name: GOPVUE
records.synthesisPrecaution: The magnetic behaviour of compounds 5, 7 and 8 are very similar and reminiscent of that of 2 and 3. Thus, there is a competition between two interactions of opposite nature which operate through the carboxylate-bridged layers of copper( ii ) ions. The two crystallographically different carboxylate bridges within the layers must couple the copper( ii ) ions ferro- and antiferromagnetically. Then, under a magnetic point of view, the layers of 5, 7 and 8 can be seen as cross-linked AF and F chains. An analysis through the Baker and Rushbrooke numerical expression for a ferromagnetically coupled copper( ii ) chain with a mean-field term to take into account the interchain interactions [eqn (1)–(3)]27,28 was performed. Least-squares best-fit parameters are g = 1.981(4), 2.076(2) and 2.055(2), J = +9.0(1), +6.3(1) and +6.8(1) cm−1, j = −1.083(8), −0.929(2) and −1.089(3) cm−1 and R = 9 × 10−4, 4 × 10−4 and 8 × 10−4 for 5, 7, and 8, respectively. Even thinking that the model fittings match well the experimental data in the whole temperature range as can be seen in Fig. 8, the values of J and j must be taken with caution due to the rough character of the approaches used. The antiferromagnetic coupling constant can be estimated from the critical field [Hc = 2.4 (5) and 1.2 T (7 and 8)] being j ~ −1.1 cm−1 for 5 and j ~ −0.6 cm−1 for 7 and 8. These values are similar to that obtained from the analysis of the antiferromagnetically coupled copper( ii ) layers in complex 6.

records.name: ISOPOV
records.synthesisPrecaution: In this review, we explain how pyrazine (hereafter as pz) leds to various structures spanning from multicomponent molecular crystals to coordination polymers. An important factor in the study of pz-based compounds is the crucial roles of the non-covalent interactions; we examined it with pz-based cocrystals and salts and also show that how purposeful selection of ligands with various functional groups can influence the physico-chemical property of the final structures. Furthermore, the CSD analysis revealed that due to the N,N′-exo-bidentate nature of pz, the probability of polymeric compounds are much more than the dimers and monomers counterparts. We also showed that pz-based coordination polymers (CPs) can be categorized into two groups; i) CPs that expanding with only pz ligand into 1D to 3D structures. ii) CPs that are constituted from pz and some auxiliary ligands in which pz linked 2D layers and created porous extended CPs and metal organic frameworks (MOFs). We presented important applications of pz-based compounds in the spin crossover systems. Finally, this review summarized some structural features of pz ligand that are useful for the design and preparation of new materials, serving as a reference in learning more about this particular area which inspired new researchers.

records.synthesisPrecaution: To a solution of [Cu(H2O)6][ClO4]2 (74.1 mg, 0.200 mmol) [warning: perchlorates can be dangerous – this procedure should not be scaled up without appropriate precautions ] in acetonitrile (3.0 ml) was added a solution of R-Pyox (0.200 mmol) in acetonitrile (3.0 ml). The resulting blue/green solution was allowed to stir for 12 h under argon before removing the volatiles under reduced pressure (Schlenk line vacuum). The solid residue was washed with diethyl ether (2 × 5 ml), extracted into acetonitrile (10 ml), filtered through Celite to remove any insoluble residues, and the solvent removed from the filtrate under reduced pressure. records.synthesisPrecaution: The behavior of (5) in the high temperature region (T > 50 K) is identical to that of (2) (Fig. 5), consistent with a similar coordination environment and single ion effects and was modeled with essentially the same parameters (g|| = 2.61, g⊥ = 2.25, D = 23 cm−1). Below 50 K, the behavior of (5) deviates from that of (2) with an upturn in χT consistent with local ferromagnetic interactions. The absence of an out of phase component in additional ac susceptibility studies (see Supplementary Information, S3 ) precludes the presence of long range order , single-chain magnetism or ferromagnetic impurities. As a consequence, the upturn (and eventual downturn below 4 K) is likely due to short range local ferromagnetic interactions. Since the back-to-back N3O2 macrocycle did not propagate magnetic exchange in (2), the difference in the magnetic response in (5) at low temperature can be attributed to either magnetic exchange between CoII centres via the diamagnetic [Fe(CN) 6]4− ion leading to discrete CoII dimers within the polymeric structure, or to through space dipolar exchange. Since the origin of the exchange interaction is uncertain, attempts to model the magnetic exchange should be viewed with caution. Nevertheless, in the simplest case of exchange coupling via the diamagnetic Fe(CN)64− bridge, a simple dimer model can be employed to gain a qualitative estimate of the strength of the magnetic exchange. Both an isotropic Heisenberg model and an anisotropic Ising spin model implementing effective S = ½ spins for the Kramer’s doublet ground state were employed to model the magnetic interactions between CoII sites, with the Ising model (Eq. 2) [20], providing a substantially improved fit consistent with the large single ion anisotropy. records.synthesisPrecaution: Oscillator strengths of the f–f transitions at 293 K and 4 K are given in Table 3a. The intensities of the 4f–4f transitions decrease with decreasing temperature. This is due to depopulation of the higher crystal field (CF) levels of the ground 4I9/2 state and electron–phonon coupling. The spectral intensities of the 4f–4f transitions show a strong dependence on the chemical environment, associated to the coordination geometry, crystal field (CF) and ligand polarizability . This strong dependence is reflected in differences in oscillator strengths of the f–f transitions (especially the hypersensitive transition) in 3Nd as compared to 1Nd and 2Nd, in which –OCH 3 groups at P atom were substituted with –OCH2C6H5 groups. Also, for the 3Nd complex the biggest decrease in intensity of the 4I9/2→4G5/2, 2G7/2 transition between room and 4 K temperature illustrating the partially vibronic nature of this transition is observed. Table 3b shows the values of Judd–Ofelt parameters. Analysis of these parameters for 1Nd, 2Nd, and 3Nd reveals the smallest changes for τ6. Parameter τ6 also has the same value for 1Nd and Na[Nd(C6H5S(O)2NP(O)(OCH3)2)4] (τ2=10.64±0.77; τ4=5.52±0.69; τ6=8.49±1.00) [12f]. This is due to the almost identical inner coordination sphere and point symmetry (close to D2d) of Nd ions. This is consistent with the calculations made by Mason and Tranter for octa-coordinated complexes [22]. They showed that the ligand polarizability contribution to Ωλ decreases from 66% to 17% and to 0.1% for Ω2, Ω4 and Ω6. The corresponding crystal-field contribution increases from 5% to 57% and to 98.5%. The difference between 1Nd and Na[Nd(C6H5S(O)2NP(O)(OCH3)2)4] is the presence of the CH3 group in the phenyl ring in the para position (1Nd), which slightly changes the polarizability of oxygen atoms bonded to the P atom and Nd–O distances. However, the significant changes in τ2 value in the series 1Nd, 2Nd, and 3Nd and Na[Nd(C6H5S(O)2NP(O)(OCH3)2)4] show the complexity of factors influencing the value of this parameter. An important factor here is the polarizability, which is different for these ligands. 3Nd complex most widely differs from the others: the inner coordination sphere, ligands polarizability, covalency and the occurrence of non-covalent interactions (π–π stacking interactions). This is reflected in the value of the τ2 parameter. Over the years, many authors have tried to find a correlation between the parameters of intensity and the chemical nature of the lanthanide compounds, but it is a complex phenomenon which is still unresolved. However, it should be emphasized that the comparison of the parameters set by the various authors (especially for crystals of compounds with low symmetry) should be approached with caution due to the high error of determined parameters, the way of measurement which should take into account the anisotropy of single crystals as well as because the values of parameters depend on the transitions which were used for the least-square fitting procedure. The Judd–Ofelt theory and the investigations on the correlation of f–f transitions in rare earths complexes were discussed in a very accessible way by Binnemans [3].

records.name: NAKCEI
records.synthesisPrecaution: In this review, we explain how pyrazine (hereafter as pz) leds to various structures spanning from multicomponent molecular crystals to coordination polymers. An important factor in the study of pz-based compounds is the crucial roles of the non-covalent interactions; we examined it with pz-based cocrystals and salts and also show that how purposeful selection of ligands with various functional groups can influence the physico-chemical property of the final structures. Furthermore, the CSD analysis revealed that due to the N,N′-exo-bidentate nature of pz, the probability of polymeric compounds are much more than the dimers and monomers counterparts. We also showed that pz-based coordination polymers (CPs) can be categorized into two groups; i) CPs that expanding with only pz ligand into 1D to 3D structures. ii) CPs that are constituted from pz and some auxiliary ligands in which pz linked 2D layers and created porous extended CPs and metal organic frameworks (MOFs). We presented important applications of pz-based compounds in the spin crossover systems. Finally, this review summarized some structural features of pz ligand that are useful for the design and preparation of new materials, serving as a reference in learning more about this particular area which inspired new researchers.

In an N2-filled VAC Atmospheres glovebox, the desolvated crystals were transferred into a 4 mL vial, which was then placed in a 20 mL vial containing excess white phosphorus. Caution: white phosphorus is highly toxic and reacts violently with O2in air. The 20 mL vial was sealed with a PTFE-lined cap then heated for 24 h at 80 °C. The P4-dosed crystals were then coated with Paratone-N oil prior to use for single-crystal X-ray diffraction experiments.

records.name: TOBQEI
records.synthesisPrecaution: Complexes 2, 4 and 5 have in common the presence of a double μ-κO:κO bridge in a dimanganese( ii ) unit. This dinuclear fragment is connected to other six dimanganese( ii ) units through monoatomic μ-κO:κO and anti–syn and syn–syn carboxylate bridges in 2 to afford a 3D structure (Fig. S1†), whereas they are interconnected to another four across anti–anti and anti–syn carboxylate bridges leading to 2D structures in 4 and 5 (see Fig. 8). In an attempt to analyze the magnetic data of these compounds, we used the simple expression for two magnetically interacting spin sextets derived from the isotropic Hamiltonian [eqn (4)], χM = [2 Ng2β2 / k ( T − θ )][ A / B ] (4) with A = x + 5 x3 + 14 x6 + 30 x10 + 55 x14 (5) B = 1 + 3 x + 5 x3 + 7 x6 + 9 x10 + 11 x15 (6) and x = exp( J / kT ) (7) In this equation, N, β and k have their usual meanings and a θ term was introduced to account for the interdimer interactions. Least-squares best-fit parameters are: J = −3.72(3) cm−1, g = 2.00(1) and θ = −0.31(5) K for 2, J = −0.835(5) cm−1, g = 2.01(1) and θ = −0.11(1) K for 4 and J = −1.115(3) cm−1, g = 2.01(1) and θ = −0.08(2) K for 5 (Fig. 12 and S4†). Although the calculated curves match well with the experimental magnetic data of the three compounds in the whole temperature range explored, it should be noted that the values of J for compounds 2 and 4–5 are very different due to the extensive interdimer magnetic pathways present in each compound: six interdimer interactions for 2 and four for 4–5. The influence of these interactions was taken into account in the model as a θ parameter. The values of the magnetic coupling obtained through the least-squares fit using this model have to be considered with caution because of the crude approximation used to determine them. It deserves to be noted that the previous magneto-structural studies with double oxo(carboxylate) bridged dicopper( ii )34 and digadolinium( iii )35 compounds have shown the occurrence of weak ferro- and antiferromagnetic interactions, with the nature of the magnetic coupling being strongly dependent on the angle at the bridgehead oxo(carboxylate) bridge.
records.conclusionBoundary: Real text-mined synthesis evidence; not a mass-balanced LCI and not a third-party-reviewed comparative LCA.

records.name: VAFFAL
records.synthesisPrecaution: Several examples of minerals are known which contain fluoride complexes bridged by alkali metals e.g. NaBF4 (ferruccite), Na3AlF6 (cryolite), K2NaAlF6 (elpasolite), Na2LiAlF6 (simmonsite). Here, it has been shown that similar structures can be targeted synthetically. Fluoride coordinated to chromium(III) interacts with protic solvents and small unpolarizable ions in solution as well as in the solid state. Efficient clustering of alkali metal cations by bridging uncharged complexes constitutes a new approach towards heterometallic systems. The pronounced tendency towards linear bridging by fluoride in these systems may render these interactions important in crystal engineering and in geometric control of polynuclear systems. Currently efforts along these lines are being undertaken. A strong effect on the auxiliary ligands by perturbation of coordinated fluoride ligands has been identified by DFT modeling. This result signals a warning regarding interpreting solvatochromism and spectral interaction with alkali metal cations in the framework of the traditional additive ligand-field models.

records.synthesisPrecaution: As can be seen in Section 2, in all the successful synthetic attempts the nitrogen heterocycle was in less than the stoichiometric amount. Initially we used 1:1:1 metal:PTCH3:Lewis base ratios. Again we were isolating products with non-reproducible C/N ratio. Only with less than the stoichiometric amount of the heterocycle the precipitation of solids proceeded smoothly and resulted in the formation of crystalline materials. In that case caution should be taken to isolate the crystalline products as soon as possible. Second and third crops of crystals isolated from the reaction mixtures were found contaminated with the same compound. Their XRPD patterns revealed the presence of a second phase which was identical to a product isolated from reaction mixtures containing zinc and 1,2,3-propane-tricarboxylic only. This product is formulated as Zn3(PTC)2·xH2O and attempts for its structural characterization are in progress.
